proofs.full_local_argument: Put w=y-bx-c. Hessian blocks are Hxx=-2mu b^2 I, Hxy=Hyx^T=2mu b I and Hyy=H_F(y)-2mu I. Thus Hyy<=-mu I. The quadratic joint Hessian has norm 2mu(1+b^2), giving ||H_f||<=mu+2mu(1+b^2)=mu(3+2b^2)=L. Integration yields joint gradient Lipschitzness. Only H_F(y) varies, so ||H_f(z)-H_f(z')||<=rho||y-y'||<=rho||z-z'||. Strong concavity gives a global negative-quadratic upper bound in y, so inner maximization is coercive and has a unique maximizer. At x=y=0, grad_y f=g0+2mu c=0, hence y*(0)=0 and Phi(0)=F(0)-mu||c||^2. Evaluating at y=bx+c gives Phi(x)>=F(bx+c)>=inf F. Conversely, for any y choose x=(y-c-grad F(y)/(2mu))/b. Then grad_y f=0, y is the unique maximizer, and Phi(x)=F(y)-||grad F(y)||^2/(4mu)<=F(y). Taking infima gives inf Phi=inf F and initial gap<=Delta. At y*, grad F(y*)=2mu(y*-u), and Danskin gives grad Phi(x)=2mu b(y*-u)=b grad F(y*). Smoothness implies ||grad F(u)||<=||grad F(y*)||+mu||u-y*||=(3/2)||grad F(y*)||=3||grad Phi(x)||/(2b). For simulation first query F at 0 to compute g0,c. At each queried y obtain F(y), grad F(y), H_F(y). Compute f=F(y)-mu||w||^2, gx=2mu b w, gy=grad F(y)-2mu w and the displayed Hessian blocks. This yields the exact adaptive transcript, including c computed after the permitted first response. Returning bxhat+c requires no output oracle call, so simulation costs at most N+1 baseline calls. For a hitting-time theorem append this output as the next baseline query, requiring a horizon of N+2 positions. Early stopping can be padded to N; unused responses need not affect output. All maps remain measurable and the success implication holds seed by seed. No minimizer or unqueried derivatives are supplied.

assumptions: F is C^2 and bounded below; F(0)-inf F<=Delta; globally ||H_F||op<=mu and H_F is rho-Lipschitz.
g0 is obtained by an actual baseline query at 0 or belongs to its permitted initial transcript. Public c contains only this returned gradient, not a minimizer or unqueried derivatives.
statement.conclusion: f has joint L-Lipschitz gradient, joint rho-Lipschitz Hessian and mu-strong concavity in y. y*(0)=0; inf Phi=inf F; Phi(0)=F(0)-||g0||^2/(4mu), hence initial gap<=Delta. For all x, ||grad F(bx+c)||<=3||grad Phi(x)||/(2b). After one origin query computes g0, one all-derivative query at y simulates one complete bundle at (x,y). N lifted calls and arbitrary primal output yield uhat=bxhat+c using at most N+1 baseline calls; if g0 was already permitted, incremental cost is N. A hitting-time interface must additionally append uhat as a query position, giving at most N+2 positions. Its no-small-gradient event through T rules out success when N+2<=T.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For F:R^d->R, set L=kappa mu, b=sqrt((kappa-3)/2), g0=grad F(0), c=-g0/(2mu), f(x,y)=F(y)-mu||y-bx-c||^2, Phi(x)=max_y f(x,y), u=bx+c.
statement.parameter_domains: Finite d>=1; mu>0, rho>=0, Delta>=0, kappa>=6; b>0; x,y in R^d.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such F and every x. Deterministic identities preserve success events pointwise; no probability convention belongs intrinsically to this lemma.
